newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico 755 MW coal-fired unit restart delayed.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico 755 MW coal-fired unit restart delayed.

text.p: Restart of the 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was delayed to Wednesday due to the discovery of a tube leak, an Arizona Public Service Co spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The unit has been down since Sunday when a booster fan failure caused it to trip off and had been expected to restart around noon Tuesday.
Four Corners unit 5 was said on Monday to be operating at 50 MW below its 750 MW level due to emissions restrictions.
The plant's three smaller units were said to be running near capacity at 186 MW, 187 MW and 244 MW.
Arizona Public Service, which operates Four Corners, owns units 1, 2, and 3 along with 15 percent of units 4 and 5.
Southern California Edison Co holds a 48 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
